about: Where the experts broadly agree on splitting a paycheck. Pebbles uses these targets automatically and checks this file online for updates.
consensus: Cover needs first, and try to keep them at or under half of take-home pay.
Save about 20% of take-home. If money is tight, keep saving something (at least 5%) so the habit and the cushion keep growing.
Build an emergency fund before other goals: one month of needs to start, then 3 to 6 months.
Aim for 15% of pre-tax pay toward retirement over time, counting any employer match. Always take the full match.
Keep housing at or below about 30% of gross income.
Whatever is left after needs and savings is yours to spend without guilt.

sources.name: 50/30/20 rule
sources.by: Elizabeth Warren & Amelia Warren Tyagi, All Your Worth
sources.summary: 50% needs, 30% wants, 20% savings and debt payoff, of after-tax income.

sources.name: 50/15/5 rule
sources.summary: Essentials at most 50% of take-home, 15% of pre-tax income to retirement (including employer match), 5% of take-home to short-term savings.

sources.name: Emergency savings
sources.summary: Three to six months of essential expenses set aside for emergencies.

sources.name: Housing cost burden
sources.by: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
sources.summary: Households paying more than 30% of income for housing are considered cost-burdened.
